claims.evidence: NHS doxazosin page: lowers high blood pressure, which can reduce risk of heart attack and stroke; eases prostate symptoms incl. urinary problems.
StatPearls Alpha-Blockers: doxazosin, prazosin, terazosin are selective alpha-1 blockers used for hypertension, second-line due to adverse effects, particularly orthostatic hypotension.

NHS doxazosin main page: works by widening blood vessels (and relaxing muscles around prostate and bladder). The first-pass verbatim 'alpha blockers reduce blood pressure by relaxing...' quote on the About page was not confirmed in returned text, so narrowed to doxazosin and re-cited.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says doxazosin lowers blood pressure by widening the blood vessels.

claims.evidence: StatPearls: selective alpha-1 blockers cause vasodilation by blocking norepinephrine at alpha-1 receptors. The 'act on the sympathetic nervous system' clause was not seen in returned text.
claims.newSentence: A StatPearls review explains that selective alpha-1 blockers widen blood vessels by stopping noradrenaline from activating alpha-1 receptors.

claims.evidence: StatPearls snippet: nonselective agents block alpha-1 and alpha-2 and combined blockade gives vasodilation; it does NOT state the norepinephrine-release or 'offset' point. That comes from a PMC review (Alpha1-Adrenergic Blockers: Current Usage Considerations): presynaptic alpha-2 receptors, which reduce norepinephrine release, are inhibited. 'Partly offset' not supported.
claims.newSentence: A review says that non-selective alpha blockers also block presynaptic alpha-2 receptors, which normally reduce the release of noradrenaline.

claims.evidence: NHS side effects of doxazosin: main ones are headaches, swollen feet/ankles/fingers, needing to pee suddenly or more often, lower stomach pain; common (more than 1 in 100), usually mild and short-lived.

NHS tamsulosin side effects: main ones are dizziness and ejaculation problems; common, usually mild. 'Little or no semen' detail not seen. Claim sits on the side-effects page, not the common-questions page.
claims.newSentence: For tamsulosin the NHS lists dizziness and problems with ejaculation as the main side effects.

claims.evidence: Doxazosin half: NHS how-and-when/common questions: dizzy especially at first or after a bigger dose; best to stop alcohol until you see how it affects you. Tamsulosin half: alcohol can increase the blood-pressure-lowering effect and cause dizziness; 'most likely when starting' not confirmed for tamsulosin. Main doxazosin page not shown to carry it.
claims.newSentence: For doxazosin, the NHS says dizziness is most likely when first starting or after a dose increase, and suggests avoiding alcohol at first; for tamsulosin it says alcohol can add to the blood-pressure-lowering effect and make dizziness worse. (cite also https://www.nhs.uk/medicines/tamsulosin/common-questions-about-tamsulosin/)

claims.evidence: MedlinePlus doxazosin: dizziness/fainting on standing is more common at start, when dose is increased, or if treatment has been stopped for MORE THAN a few days. Sentence dropped 'more than'.
claims.newSentence: MedlinePlus says dizziness on standing up quickly is more common with doxazosin when treatment starts, when the dose is increased, or when treatment has been stopped for more than a few days.

claims.evidence: NHS tamsulosin guidance: tell the doctor in advance if having cataract or glaucoma surgery, as tamsulosin may cause complications during the operation. Carried by the who-can-and-cannot / common-questions pages; not shown on the main page. Do not add the 1-2 weeks stop timing.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says anyone due to have cataract or glaucoma surgery should tell the doctor in advance, because tamsulosin may cause complications during the operation.

claims.evidence: NHS: tell a doctor or pharmacist if taking erectile dysfunction medicines such as sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil; listed as interacting medicines on the interactions page.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says to tell a doctor or pharmacist about medicines for erectile dysfunction, such as sildenafil, tadalafil or vardenafil, when taking tamsulosin.

claims.evidence: NHS how-and-when pages for tamsulosin and doxazosin: an extra dose can be dangerous (lower blood pressure, faster heart rate); if more than prescribed has been taken, call NHS 111. First-pass URLs (main page, common questions) were not the pages carrying it.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says to call NHS 111 after taking more than the prescribed amount of tamsulosin or doxazosin, because an extra dose can lower blood pressure and raise heart rate. (cite https://www.nhs.uk/medicines/tamsulosin/how-and-when-to-take-tamsulosin/ and https://www.nhs.uk/medicines/doxazosin/how-and-when-to-take-doxazosin/)

notes: Several URLs in the ledger were not the pages carrying the claim; corrected in each url field. c08 and c12 combine two NHS pages and now name both. No doses present. StatPearls alpha-2/noradrenaline-release wording was not found in StatPearls; use the PMC review or drop. Searches used: 12 for this class (20 for both classes).
